findings.title: [P1] Restrict login redirects to trusted destinations
findings.body: When `returnUrl` is influenced by login-request input, passing it directly to `location.assign` permits absolute or protocol-relative attacker URLs, enabling phishing through the trusted login flow. Validate it and restrict navigation to an allowed same-origin path.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to audit output
findings.body: Every issued bearer token is passed as audit detail and written with `console.log`. In deployments that retain or aggregate console output, anyone with log access can recover unexpired credentials and impersonate their holders. Log only non-sensitive metadata or a non-reversible identifier.

findings.title: [P3] Preserve the fallback for whitespace-only cached names
findings.body: For a whitespace-only cache entry, `trim()` produces `""`, but the nullish fallback does not apply. Callers therefore receive an empty display name instead of `"Anonymous"`. Apply the fallback after normalization when the result is empty.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to audit output
findings.body:
Every call passes the raw token to `console.log`. In environments where console output is retained or centrally collected, anyone with log access can recover bearer credentials and impersonate users until those tokens expire.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restrict login redirects to trusted same-origin destinations
findings.body:
If an attacker can influence `returnUrl`, values such as `https://evil.example/` or `//evil.example/` redirect users away from the application immediately after login, enabling phishing through a trusted login flow. Previously the destination was fixed to `/dashboard`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restrict login redirects to trusted same-origin URLs
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` comes from a query parameter or other attacker-controlled input, values such as `https://evil.example` create an authentication-flow open redirect. Browsers may also execute a `javascript:` URL in the page origin when CSP permits it, turning this into DOM XSS.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Stop logging issued tokens in plaintext
findings.body:
Every call records the bearer token through `console.log`. In deployments that collect stdout or expose browser/server consoles, anyone with log access can recover an unexpired token and impersonate its holder.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
